telegram:defapress_ir/59783.summary_en: The 60mm mortar: an influential factor in close-range warfare. The 60mm mortar is one of the lightest and most widely used types of mortar in the arsenals of military forces worldwide. This weapon plays a vital role in providing direct fire support due to its low weight, ease of transport by infantry, and appropriate destructive power for close targets. The 60mm mortar is typically distributed at the platoon or even infantry squad level. Unlike heavier mortars (such as 81 or 120mm) which require vehicles or large teams, a team of two to three people can carry this weapon and prepare it for firing in less than a few minutes. The main purpose of its deployment is the destruction of targets.

Bloomberg wrote: India has again, due to worsening losses at the country's refineries following Iran's war, increased the price of liquefied gas. This is the second time since the start of Iran's war that India has increased the price of domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG); an action taken with the aim of reducing losses for state-owned fuel distribution companies and offsetting the costs resulting from subsidised sales. Brigadier General Sayed Reza Mortazavian, head of Shahid Sadoughi Hospital in Isfahan affiliated with the IRGC Ground Forces, announced the deployment and commencement of operations of this force's super-specialised mobile hospital on Pasdaran Boulevard in the city of Qom. Given the significant presence of those accompanying the pure body of the great leader of the revolution, this 64-bed mobile hospital with a capacity of 85 specialised and support personnel has been deployed on site and is ready to provide medical services to ceremony participants. The hospital is equipped with two specialised operating theatres, laboratory, and radiological imaging facilities.
